G2.rationale: The paper's stated priority is the application of the Q Trait function to AD and cognitive g. The first principal quantitative result reported is the Q Trait statistic for educational attainment in the AD analysis (Q Trait(2)=36.75), which is the first row of Table 1 and the first result in the Results section.

quotes.quote: the exact version of the Q Trait function used, along with input data and scripts, has been archived on Zenodo (DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17186083 )

G3.rationale: The Zenodo deposit contains LDSC_ADGWAX_QTRAIT.RData and LDSC_G_FACTOR_QTRAIT.RData, which are the LDSC-derived genetic covariance matrices (S and V) that serve as the analysis inputs for the Q Trait function. These are minimally processed inputs, not the outputs of the Q Trait analysis.

quotes.quote: A χ 2 difference test is used to compare the common and independent pathways models, as indicated by the Q Trait heterogeneity index, which follows a χ 2 distribution with K − 1 degrees of freedom (where K represents the number of indicator traits loading on the common factor).

G4.rationale: The paper describes the Q Trait statistic as a chi-square difference test between common and independent pathways models, and the lSRMR as the root mean square of residual genetic correlations. The method is described well enough to implement without the original code.
